regions: Mexico, Central America and the Caribbean

folk.name: The lost Cartographer
folk.place: High fells near Scafell Pike, Lake District
folk.riddle: High on the roof of England, among crags and screes, a mapmaker sits with half a map and no idea which way is down.

trails.clue: The Cartographer has dropped a page. It blew east, over the Pennines, to a green road where a pedlar walks his donkey above the Vale of York.

folk.name: Pedlar and donkey
folk.place: The old drove road over the Hambleton Hills, North Yorkshire
folk.riddle: Where Scots cattle once tramped south along a green road on the hill tops above Thirsk, a pedlar walks his patient donkey.

trails.clue: The pedlar picked up the page and swapped it for a goose egg with a monk in the valley below. The goose was not consulted.

folk.name: The monk and the runaway goose
folk.riddle: In a quiet valley of the Rye, below the great roofless abbey, a monk has lost all dignity chasing a goose.

trails.clue: The page is not here: the monk used it to wrap a gift for a shepherd far to the south-west, on a granite moor.

folk.name: Shepherd seeking one lost sheep
folk.riddle: Under the granite tor most climbed on the moor, a shepherd counts his flock and counts again: one is missing.

trails.clue: The shepherd tucked the page into his lost sheep's fleece for safe keeping. Now find the sheep.

folk.name: The lost sheep
folk.riddle: The shepherd of Haytor will not rest: his stray grazes alone by a tor named for a pack of hounds turned to stone.

trails.clue: The page fell out by a stone hound. A traveller took it north to a bridge the Devil built over the Lune, and paid the toll with it.

folk.name: Hedge-witch at the holy well
folk.riddle: At the well that has drawn pilgrims for thirteen hundred years, a hedge-witch stirs something green and does not share the recipe.

folk.name: A witch on Pendle Hill
folk.riddle: On the big end of the hill that gave its name to a famous trial, a cauldron bubbles by the summit wall.

folk.name: Sea captain rowing up the river
folk.riddle: His ship is far behind him, but a bearded captain still rows upstream past the old naval college, determined to reach London by oar.

folk.name: The toll-troll
folk.riddle: Under the three ribbed arches over the Lune, said to be the Devil's own work, someone large and grey charges a penny a crossing.

trails.clue: The troll cannot read and sent the page south in a hurry. It ended under a dragon asleep round a roundabout. Good luck.

folk.name: Highwaymen on the heath
folk.riddle: "Stand and deliver!" On the heath once feared by every coach out of London, two shady figures wait with a lantern and a blade.

folk.name: The sulking serpent
folk.riddle: Off the ruined castle on the long dark loch, three humps and a sulky face: it is tired of being photographed.

folk.name: Smugglers in the cove
folk.riddle: In the cove named after a smuggler who called himself a king, barrels come ashore by lantern light.

folk.name: A wolf pack eyeing a village
folk.riddle: Legend says the last wolf in Scotland was killed by the Findhorn. Three more are watching the village, all the same.

folk.name: The knight and the cross little dragon
folk.riddle: At the mouth of the cave where a witch was turned to stone, a very small knight has met a very cross lizard.

trails.clue: The last of them was beaten on a flat hill below a white horse. Find the saint.

folk.name: Here be Roundabouts
folk.riddle: Here be roundabouts. A great green dragon sleeps curled round one on the edge of a famous Berkshire town, and a tiny knight dare not wake it.

trails.clue: You found every page. The map is whole again. The Cartographer thanks you, and asks if you know the way down.

folk.name: Wayland the Smith
folk.riddle: Leave your horse and a silver coin by the long barrow on the Ridgeway, and the smith of legend will shoe it by morning.

folk.name: Herne the Hunter
folk.riddle: An antlered rider with a hound and a horn haunts the oaks of the royal park by the castle. Keep to the paths.

folk.name: The barrow-wight
folk.riddle: A pale crowned figure keeps the long barrow above the Kennet, where the dead of five thousand years ago were laid.

folk.name: The wodewose
folk.riddle: Among stunted mossy oaks and tumbled granite in the West Dart valley, a hairy wild man of the woods leans on his club.

folk.name: Orcs camped on the moor
folk.riddle: On the bleakest moor in Scotland, all bog and lochan and sky, a tusked warband warms itself at a smoky fire.

folk.name: The giant out for a walk
folk.riddle: The chalk giant on the hillside has a cousin, fully dressed, striding over the downs above the village.

folk.name: The unicorn of the glen
folk.riddle: The kingdom's own beast grazes quietly where the glen is deepest, under the Three Sisters.

folk.name: The mermaid of Zennor
folk.riddle: She lured a chorister of St Senara's down to the sea; she sits on a rock in the cove below the church to this day.

folk.name: Will-o'-the-wisp
folk.riddle: Lights over the last wild fen. Do not follow them across the sedge.

folk.name: Fairy ring on the downs
folk.riddle: On the high chalk downs above the Weald, a ring of red toadstools and two very small dancers.

folk.name: The cockatrice in the ruins
folk.riddle: Half cockerel, half serpent, wholly bad tempered: it roosts in the slighted ruins in the gap of the Purbeck hills.

folk.name: Wyvern over Wales
folk.riddle: Where a red dragon and a white were found fighting under a hill fort, a red wyvern still circles.

trails.clue: A smaller one lives in a Somerset cave. A very small knight has found it.

folk.name: The giant at the causeway
folk.riddle: A giant who built a road of stone columns across the sea to Scotland is out on the causeway again.

folk.name: Black Shuck
folk.riddle: A huge black dog with one fiery eye pads the cliff path along the north Norfolk coast. Do not look back.

folk.name: Knockers in the tin mine
folk.riddle: By the engine houses on the cliffs of the far west, the little knockers of the mines tap and tap.

folk.name: The selkie
folk.riddle: By the Stone Age village in the bay, someone has left a sealskin on the rocks and is sitting very still.

folk.name: The kelpie
folk.riddle: A grey horse with a weedy mane waits in the shallows of the bonnie loch. Do not climb on.

folk.name: The banshee
folk.riddle: At the castle said to be the most haunted in Ireland, a pale woman keens on the hill.

folk.name: The little shoemaker
folk.riddle: On the mountain of the old stories a tiny cobbler taps away beside his pots. If you catch him, do not look away.

folk.name: The brownie
folk.riddle: At the old house in the Borders where the gates stay shut, a little helper sweeps the yard at night.

folk.name: The Green Man
folk.riddle: The chapel is carved with a hundred leafy faces. One has stepped outside into the glen.

folk.name: Ghost knight at Bosworth
folk.riddle: A pale knight still walks the field where the last English king to die in battle fell.

folk.name: Halflings at a picnic
folk.riddle: Below the folly on the Cotswold edge, a family of small folk has spread a cloth: second breakfast.

folk.name: The runaway cheese
folk.riddle: On the steepest slope in the Cotswolds a cheese is winning the race. A small person in red is losing.

folk.name: The halfling and the heron
folk.riddle: On the little packhorse bridge over Barrow Beck, a halfling dangles a line while a heron eyes the catch.

folk.name: A nap in the orchard
folk.place: Cider orchards near Much Marcle, Herefordshire
folk.riddle: Among the apple trees of the cider country, someone small has had too much of last year's pressing.

folk.name: The dragon of the hoard
folk.riddle: By the royal burial mounds above the Deben, a dragon sleeps on the gold the diggers did not find.

trails.clue: In Wales, a red one still circles the hill where two dragons were found fighting.

folk.name: The Merry Maidens' piper
folk.riddle: Nineteen maidens danced on the Sabbath and were turned to stone; their piper is still playing nearby.

folk.name: Surveying the Long Man
folk.place: The Long Man of Wilmington, East Sussex
folk.riddle: A surveyor with map and staff is measuring the tall outline on the downs. He has counted to sixty metres and given up.

folk.name: Saint George on Dragon Hill
folk.riddle: Grass will not grow where the dragon's blood was spilt, they say, on the flat hill below the White Horse.

trails.clue: Every dragon found. Saint George is relieved; the dragons less so.

folk.name: An outlaw in the greenwood
folk.riddle: Under the great oak of the forest, a hooded archer in green takes aim. Guess who.

folk.name: Longship off Holy Island
folk.riddle: Off the holy island of the north-east, a striped sail. The monks will not like this.

trails.clue: The longship sails north to the island whirlpool, where something with many arms waits.

folk.name: Monks of Lindisfarne
folk.riddle: Beside the priory where a famous gospel book was made, a monk hurries indoors with a book under his arm.

folk.name: A Viking in Jorvik
folk.riddle: In the old Norse town on the Ouse, under the street called the cup-makers' way, a bearded settler strolls.

folk.name: The abbess's nun
folk.riddle: On the headland of the 199 steps, a nun of Abbess Hild's house carries a candle against the sea wind.

folk.name: Monk at Durham
folk.riddle: On the rock in the loop of the Wear, a monk of the cathedral priory carries a lantern for Saint Cuthbert.

folk.name: Pilgrims riding to Canterbury
folk.riddle: They tell each other stories all the way from Southwark; this one has reached the city of the martyr at last.

trails.clue: From the shrine of the martyr, cross the sea and find the hill in Burgundy where crusades were preached.

folk.name: Piper on the Mile
folk.riddle: Between the castle on its rock and the palace at the bottom, a piper fills the old town with noise.

folk.name: Fairies in the glen
folk.place: The Fairy Glen, Uig, Isle of Skye
folk.riddle: Little cones of green hills, rings of stones, and something very small dancing in Skye's smallest glen.

folk.name: Knight at Bamburgh
folk.riddle: Below the great fortress on its rock above the dunes, a knight rides out under his banner.

folk.name: Watchman at Clitheroe
folk.riddle: On the limestone knoll above the little Lancashire town, by one of the smallest keeps in England, a watchman stands his post.

folk.name: Falconer at the cove
folk.riddle: Where peregrines nest on a great curved cliff of limestone, a falconer has come to admire the competition.

folk.name: Monk on the Tor
folk.riddle: On the green hill with the lonely tower above the Somerset Levels, a monk climbs towards the old chapel of Saint Michael.

folk.name: Bladud's swineherd
folk.riddle: A prince with an ailment kept pigs, the story goes, and found the hot springs when his pigs wallowed. His swine are still near the abbey.

folk.name: The Lambton Worm
folk.riddle: A worm that grew too big for its well wound itself round a hill by the Wear. A temple stands there now, but the worm has not left.

folk.name: Gelert the faithful hound
folk.riddle: In the village where the rivers meet, a faithful hound waits by a prince's grave.

folk.name: The Lady of the Lake
folk.riddle: Under the dark scarp of the Black Mountain, a lady stands at the edge of a small lake. She once married a farmer here.

folk.name: The fair folk at Brú na Bóinne
folk.riddle: The great mound by the Boyne was a house of the gods, they say. Its people still dance on the grass outside.

folk.name: Monk on the Rock
folk.riddle: On the rock the Devil bit out of a mountain, a monk rings a bell among the ruins of the kings of Munster.

folk.name: Monk of Skellig
folk.riddle: Six hundred steps up a needle of rock in the Atlantic, a monk climbs to his beehive cell.

folk.name: Hermit of the glen of two lakes
folk.riddle: A holy man left the world for a cave above the upper lake. A blackbird nested in his open hand, they say.

folk.name: At the Fairy Bridge
folk.place: The Fairy Bridge, Isle of Man
folk.riddle: Say hello to the little people as you cross the bridge on the road from Douglas, or bad luck will follow.

folk.name: Watchman at Mont Orgueil
folk.riddle: Above the harbour at Gorey, a watchman looks east towards Normandy from the proud mountain of a castle.

folk.name: Shepherd under Helvellyn
folk.riddle: Below the great fell with the knife-edge ridge, a shepherd brings the flock down to Ullswater.

folk.name: A giant with a bluestone
folk.riddle: The old story says giants carried the stones from far away. One of them is still looking for a spot.

folk.name: Dancers in the great circle
folk.riddle: Inside the biggest stone circle of all, with a village in the middle, a ring of toadstools has a circle of its own.

folk.name: A miner of the Dales
folk.riddle: Beneath the flat-topped mountain of the Dales, someone with a pick has found the way into the hill.

folk.name: Pilgrims to Walsingham
folk.riddle: Barefoot along the holy mile to England's Nazareth, two pilgrims with staffs and scallop shells.

folk.name: Watcher at Tintagel
folk.riddle: On the headland of a king who may never have been, a guard watches the Atlantic for ships that never come.

folk.name: On the Wall
folk.riddle: Long after the legions left, a lonely guard still walks the great wall across the north.

folk.name: Hermit in the gorge
folk.riddle: In the deepest gorge in Britain, where a famous cheese was once kept cool in the caves, a hermit sits with his lantern.

folk.name: Keening on the cliffs
folk.riddle: Two hundred metres above the Atlantic on the edge of Clare, a pale figure in the wind.

folk.name: A warband on Kinder
folk.riddle: Among the peat groughs on the dark plateau where ramblers once trespassed, an ugly camp has been pitched.

folk.name: Archer at Stanage
folk.riddle: Along the gritstone edge where millstones lie abandoned, an outlaw practises in Hathersage country.

folk.name: The beast of the moor
folk.riddle: Something large and black is seen on Cornwall's high moor, near the Cheesewring's stacked rocks.

folk.name: Scholar at Oxford
folk.riddle: In the city of dreaming spires, a scholar hurries past the great domed library, late for a lecture.

folk.name: Scholar at Cambridge
folk.riddle: Under the pinnacles of the famous chapel on the Cam, a student in a long gown clutches a book.

folk.name: The miller of Cley
folk.riddle: By the windmill above the salt marshes of the north Norfolk coast, a dusty miller heaves a sack.

folk.name: A Sussex vintner
folk.place: The vineyards of the South Downs, Sussex
folk.riddle: English wine is not a new idea: the monks had vines. A vintner picks grapes on a chalk slope in the Weald.

folk.name: Pedlar at Ludlow
folk.riddle: Below the castle of the Marches and the tall church tower, a pedlar comes into town for market day.

folk.name: Knight at Conwy
folk.riddle: By the eight towers on the estuary, a knight under a banner rides out of the walled town.

folk.name: Guard at Caernarfon
folk.riddle: By the castle with banded walls by the Menai, a guard keeps an eye on the strait.

folk.name: Skaters on the frozen fen
folk.riddle: When the fens freeze hard, the old fen skaters come out on the washes by the Ouse.

folk.name: Ploughing the open field
folk.riddle: In the last village in England still farmed in open strips, a ploughman drives his ox along a furlong.

folk.name: Goose girl at the fair
folk.riddle: Geese were once walked to the great October fair here; this girl and her flock are still on their way.

folk.name: Dairymaid of the dale
folk.riddle: In the dale of a famous crumbly cheese, a milkmaid carries her pails home along the green road.

folk.name: Pilgrims on the Camino
folk.riddle: On the last great climb of the Way of Saint James, where the old round thatched houses stand, two pilgrims plod on with their shells.

trails.clue: Only a few days more, to the city of the apostle.

folk.name: Pilgrims arrive
folk.riddle: At journey's end, in front of the great cathedral of the apostle, two pilgrims have finally stopped walking.

trails.clue: Journey's end. Some pilgrims walk on to the sea at the end of the world. You may rest.

folk.name: Over the pass
folk.riddle: Over the pass where a famous horn was blown in vain, a pilgrim on a mule comes down into Spain.

trails.clue: Westward across Spain to the last great climb, where the thatched round houses stand.

folk.name: Setting out from Le Puy
folk.riddle: Among the volcanic needles topped with chapels, two pilgrims set out on the long road south-west.

trails.clue: Over the Pyrenees by the pass where a hero blew his horn too late.

folk.name: From Vézelay
folk.riddle: From the basilica on its hill in Burgundy, where crusades were preached, pilgrims walk down to the road.

trails.clue: Walk south to the town of volcanic needles where a chapel stands on a rock.

folk.name: Crossing the bay
folk.riddle: Two pilgrims hurry across the sands towards the abbey on its island before the tide comes in like a galloping horse.

folk.name: Knight at Carcassonne
folk.riddle: Under the double walls and fifty-two towers of the fairy-tale city, a knight rides out.

folk.name: Scholar on the Île de la Cité
folk.riddle: Under the twin towers by the Seine, a scholar of the schools of Paris argues with nobody in particular.

folk.name: Lights in Brocéliande
folk.riddle: In the forest of an enchanter of legend, lights drift over the pools at dusk.

folk.name: The singer on the rock
folk.riddle: High above the narrowest bend of the Rhine a fair singer combs her hair, and boatmen forget to steer.

folk.name: Witch on the Brocken
folk.riddle: On the bald summit of the Harz where witches gather on Walpurgis night, one has come early to get the cauldron going.

folk.name: Dwarf smiths of the Harz
folk.riddle: Under the hill that gave a thousand years of silver and copper, small bearded smiths hammer by the forge.

folk.name: The piper and the rats
folk.riddle: In the town on the Weser that would not pay its bill, a piper in red and yellow leads a parade of rats.

folk.name: The town musicians
folk.riddle: A donkey, a dog, a cat and a cockerel set out to make music in this Hanseatic city and never quite arrived.

folk.name: Woodcutter of the Black Forest
folk.riddle: Among the dark firs where cuckoo clocks are carved, a woodcutter swings his axe.

folk.name: The swan knight
folk.riddle: Below the white castle of a dreaming king, a knight under a banner rides along the lake.

folk.name: Skaters at the windmills
folk.riddle: Nineteen windmills drain the polder; when the canals freeze, everyone in the village is out on the ice.

folk.name: Miller of the Zaan
folk.riddle: Among the green wooden houses and windmills on the Zaan, a dusty miller shoulders a sack.

folk.name: Merchant of Bruges
folk.riddle: In the great cloth town on its canals, a merchant in a red hood has just done very well at the market.

folk.name: Alphorn on the Rigi
folk.riddle: On the queen of mountains above the lake of the four cantons, a long low note rolls across the valley.

folk.name: The tatzelwurm
folk.riddle: A stumpy-legged worm with a cat's face lives under the alpine stones of the Kaisergebirge. Herders swear to it.

folk.name: Griffin on the peak
folk.riddle: Half eagle, half lion, guarding gold under the most famous pyramid of rock in the Alps.

folk.name: Salt miner of Hallstatt
folk.riddle: Above the lake village where salt has been mined for seven thousand years, a miner heads into the mountain.

folk.name: Gondolier
folk.riddle: Under the Rialto bridge a gondolier leans on his oar. He has heard every song.

trails.clue: A Venetian merchant set out east. Follow him to a great stone inn a day out of Konya.

folk.name: The friar and the wolf
folk.riddle: A wolf terrorised this hill town until a friar from Assisi had a word with it. They have been friends ever since.

folk.name: Pilgrim in Rome
folk.riddle: All roads lead here. Two pilgrims have walked from the north to stand in the great colonnaded square.

folk.name: A guard of the smallest state
folk.riddle: In the smallest country in the world, a guard in a striped uniform keeps the gate by the gardens.

folk.name: Wolves in the Apennines
folk.riddle: In the high national park where wolves never died out, a pack watches the village from the beech woods.

folk.name: Monster of the strait
folk.riddle: Between the rock and the whirlpool, sailors of old met a monster with many arms. Keep to the middle.

folk.name: Tilting at windmills
folk.place: The windmills of Consuegra, La Mancha
folk.riddle: On the ridge of white windmills in La Mancha, a thin knight on a thinner horse charges at a giant. His squire sighs.

folk.name: Swordsmith of Toledo
folk.riddle: In the city on the Tagus famous for its blades, a smith tests an edge on the anvil.

folk.name: Minstrel at the Alhambra
folk.riddle: In the red palace above Granada, a minstrel plays beside fountains that sing back.

folk.name: Navigator at Belém
folk.riddle: From the tower on the Tagus the great voyages set out. A ship with a red cross on its sail heads for the open sea.

folk.name: Monks of the Meteora
folk.riddle: Monasteries perch on pillars of rock in mid-air; one monk has come down for supplies and dreads the climb.

folk.name: Shepherd on Olympus
folk.riddle: On the mountain of the gods, a shepherd minds his flock and pays the gods no attention.

folk.name: Kraken of the Maelstrom
folk.riddle: Off the end of the islands where the great whirlpool turns, many arms rise from the sea.

trails.clue: West past Iceland to the icebergs of Disko Bay, where a hunter paddles a kayak.

folk.name: Longship in the fjord
folk.riddle: In the longest and deepest fjord of Norway, a striped sail glides between walls of rock.

folk.name: Trolls at the ladder
folk.riddle: Where the road climbs the troll's ladder in hairpin bends, a troll has come down to watch the traffic.

folk.name: The dragon in the king's mound
folk.riddle: By the great royal mounds of the old kings of the Swedes, a dragon guards a hoard, as dragons in the old poems do.

trails.clue: Its own cousin crossed the North Sea to sleep by a ship burial in Suffolk.

folk.name: Reindeer herder of Sápmi
folk.riddle: Just north of the Arctic Circle, where a winter market has been held for four hundred years, a herder walks with his reindeer.

folk.name: A brooding prince
folk.riddle: On the battlements of the castle at the narrows of the Sound, a young man in black is having a very bad week.

folk.name: Trolls turned to stone
folk.riddle: They were dragging a ship ashore when the sun rose. Now they stand in the sea off the black beach for ever.

folk.name: At the Law Rock
folk.riddle: Where the old parliament of the north met in a rift between two continents, a chieftain waits to speak.

folk.name: Herder by the Arctic Circle
folk.riddle: Where the Kemi meets the Ounas on the edge of the Arctic, a herder brings his reindeer through the snow.

folk.name: The Wawel dragon
folk.riddle: In a cave under the royal castle by the Vistula lived a dragon, until a cobbler fed it a sheep stuffed with sulphur.

trails.clue: This dragon has a cousin who sleeps on a hoard by the mounds of the old Swedish kings.

folk.name: Knight of the castle on the Nogat
folk.riddle: By the largest brick castle in the world, a knight in a white surcoat with a black cross rides out.

folk.name: Silver miner of Kuttenberg
folk.riddle: In the silver town whose mines paid for a kingdom and a cathedral of the miners, a miner in white heads down the shaft.

folk.name: Minstrel on the bridge
folk.riddle: Among the statues of the old stone bridge over the Vltava, a minstrel sings for a coin.

folk.name: The jester of Krumlov
folk.riddle: In the castle town in the loop of the Vltava, a jester in red and gold tumbles over the cobbles.

folk.name: Horse archer of the puszta
folk.riddle: Across the flat great plain of the Hortobágy, a horseman draws his bow at full gallop.

folk.name: Shepherd in the Carpathians
folk.riddle: High in the Carpathians above the old castle road, a shepherd and his flock graze the summer pastures.

folk.name: Monk of Rila
folk.riddle: In the striped arcades of the great monastery deep in the mountains, a monk walks to prayer.

folk.name: Merchant of Ragusa
folk.riddle: Inside the white walls of the old merchant republic, a trader counts his luck.

folk.name: At the old bridge
folk.riddle: By the high single arch over the green Neretva, a pedlar and his donkey rest before the climb.

folk.name: Baba Yaga's hut
folk.riddle: Deep in the birch and pine north of Moscow, a hut turns round on two great bird legs. Say the right words.

folk.name: The firebird
folk.riddle: Among the white monasteries and onion domes of the old town, a bird of flame has landed in the orchard.

folk.name: Sledge to Kizhi
folk.riddle: Across the frozen lake to the wooden church with twenty-two domes, a sledge is pulled over the ice.

folk.name: Cossack of the island
folk.riddle: On the rocky island in the Dnipro where the Cossack host had its stronghold, a rider waves his sabre.

folk.name: Monk of the caves
folk.riddle: Above the Dnipro, where monks once lived in caves under the hill, a monk carries a lantern below ground.

folk.name: Knight of Malta
folk.riddle: In the fortress city built after the great siege, a knight in red with a white cross rides by.

folk.name: Caravan at Sultanhanı
folk.riddle: A day's camel walk out of Konya on the road to Aksaray, a caravan reaches the great stone inn for the night.

trails.clue: East again, across Persia to a fortified inn on the salt desert road to Isfahan.

folk.name: At the island castle
folk.riddle: On an island in Lake Galvė, a guard of the grand dukes looks out across the water.

folk.name: Hanseatic merchant
folk.riddle: In the walled Hanseatic town above the Baltic, a merchant has a cart full of furs and wax.

folk.name: Samurai on the castle road
folk.riddle: On the road below the white heron castle, a samurai walks with one hand on his sword.

folk.name: Ninja on the roof
folk.riddle: In the old home of the shinobi among the hills of Iga, someone in black is crouching on a roof. You probably will not see them.

folk.name: Pilgrim on the Kumano Kodo
folk.riddle: On the old pilgrim paths through the cedar forests of the Kii mountains, a pilgrim in white walks to the great shrine.

folk.name: Rice farmer near Kyoto
folk.riddle: In the quiet valley north of the old capital, a farmer in a straw hat bends to the paddy.

folk.name: Scholar on the bridge
folk.riddle: On a humpbacked bridge in the city of gardens and canals, a scholar stops to compose a poem.

trails.clue: The silk has arrived. The scholar would like to know who ordered it.

folk.name: Watch on the Great Wall
folk.riddle: Along the wall that snakes over the hills north of Beijing, a guard walks between the watchtowers.

folk.name: Rice terraces of Longji
folk.riddle: On the dragon's backbone terraces, a farmer in a conical hat works with a water buffalo.

folk.name: Merchant on the Silk Road
folk.riddle: By the caves of a thousand buddhas on the edge of the desert, a merchant leads a two-humped camel west.

trails.clue: Down to the city of gardens and canals where a scholar composes on a bridge.

folk.name: Boatman on the Li
folk.place: The Li River at Xingping, Guangxi
folk.riddle: Among the limestone peaks of the Li, a boatman poles his little craft downstream.

folk.name: Mongol horse archer
folk.riddle: By the walls of the monastery on the site of the great khans' capital, a horse archer turns in the saddle to shoot.

folk.name: Scholar of Seoul
folk.riddle: Before the great palace of the Joseon kings, a scholar in a wide black hat walks with his fan.

folk.name: Hunter in a kayak
folk.riddle: Among the icebergs that drift out of the ice fjord, a hunter paddles a skin kayak.

trails.clue: South and inland, to voyageurs singing on the old fur route.
